newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield rises to 22.67 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yield rises to 22.67 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 128 basis points to 22.67 percent in Tuesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 37.4 billion bolivars of 177- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 21.39 percent coupon for a price of 99.43 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 21.40 percent.

The bank also sold 7.6 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 21.97 percent coupon at a price of 98.41 percent, and 6.4 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 22.54 percent coupon at an average price of 97.50 percent.
Yields for these notes rose 81 basis points to 24.49 percent for 269-day bills, and 81 basis points to 25.70 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
